generation_rule: Roles generated only after Stage-A signature freeze; no role definition uses a classical numerical target or Euclidean comparison.
independence_notes: R2 and R3 are defined from different S3 structures (cover fibers versus group action) and are not assumed equal.
R4 is scalar-valued and depends on norm/valuation optimization; it is type-incomparable with the permutation roles before any extra readout.
R5 is a quotient of an algebraic kernel and explicitly preserves the generator-orientation ambiguity.
R1 is finite/refinement-native and does not require an affine or scalar carrier.

roles.choice_dependence: No basepoint choice. Existence and refinement compatibility depend on boundary parity/refinement class.
degeneracies: non-manifold boundary without a cyclic successor
roles.exact_construction: Let s_B be the orientation-induced successor permutation on a finite boundary component B and m=|B|. If m is even, define h_B = s_B^(m/2).
roles.existence_theorem_or_failure: Exists iff m is even. It fails on odd boundary cycles.
roles.invariance_theorem_or_failure: Invariant under orientation-preserving cellular isomorphism; replacing s_B by s_B^{-1} leaves h_B unchanged because m is even.
roles.role_predicate: h lies in <s_B>, h != id, and h^2=id. Equivalently, h is the unique nonidentity involution of <s_B>.
signature_dependency: finite boundary component B with even cardinality m
roles.uniqueness_theorem_or_counterexample: Unique because a finite cyclic group of even order has exactly one element of order two.
roles.why_not_classical_formula_renaming: The construction uses only a finite cyclic successor and parity. It has no metric, circle, radius, circumference, area, angular scalar, or continuous parameter.

degeneracies: fiber cardinality not equal to two

dependency_graph.delta_q: N0-definable permutation; used as role object without scalarization

roles.exact_construction: For d in ODir, define delta_q(d) to be the unique other element of the two-element fiber q^{-1}(q(d)).
roles.existence_theorem_or_failure: Always exists in S3 by exact two-sheeting.
roles.finite_computability: EXACT_FINITE whenever ODir is finite; symbolically definable otherwise.
roles.invariance_theorem_or_failure: For every S3 isomorphism f of ODir covers, f delta_q f^{-1}=delta_q'.
roles.role_predicate: q∘delta=q, delta^2=id, and delta has no fixed points.
signature_dependency: S3_DIRACT2 or any refinement preserving its two-sheet direction cover
roles.uniqueness_theorem_or_counterexample: Unique fixed-point-free vertical involution because each q-fiber has exactly two elements.
roles.why_not_classical_formula_renaming: It is the deck transformation of a typed finite fiber relation. No scalar angle or metric quantity occurs.

roles.choice_dependence: NONE for gamma; its coupling to q is intentionally unspecified.
degeneracies: nonfaithful actions can collapse gamma to identity if S3 faithfulness is removed
groups without a unique nonidentity involution fall outside S3
roles.exact_construction: Let z be the unique nonidentity element of G satisfying z^2=e. Define gamma = rho(z).
roles.invariance_theorem_or_failure: Invariant/equivariant under S3 isomorphisms because z is uniquely definable and rho is part of the signature.
roles.role_predicate: gamma is the action image under rho of the uniquely characterized nonidentity involution of G.
roles.uniqueness_theorem_or_counterexample: The role gamma is unique, but S3 does not force gamma=delta_q.
roles.why_not_classical_formula_renaming: The role is selected by an internal group-theoretic property and an action, with no geometric scalar or numerical target.

roles.choice_dependence: Rescaling mu by c>0 sends J to J/c; changing N can also change J. These are declared structure freedoms, not hidden choices.
roles.codomain_type: Cut(K)_nonnegative, the Dedekind order-completion/readout of K
degeneracies: mu(C)=0 on nondegenerate C (excluded by S5)

dependency_graph.Per_N: N0-definable from N and finite edge lists

roles.exact_construction: For each nondegenerate convex polygon C, let Q(C)=Per_N(C)^2 / mu(C), where Per_N is the sum of edge norms. Define J_N,mu = inf_C Q(C) in Cut(K). No normalization factor is inserted.
roles.existence_theorem_or_failure: Exists uniquely in Cut(K): the ratio set is nonempty and bounded below by zero.
roles.finite_computability: Individual polygon ratios are exact finite expressions; the global infimum is generally not finite-computable without extra theorems.
roles.invariance_theorem_or_failure: Invariant under exact S5 automorphisms preserving N and mu.
roles.role_predicate: J is the greatest lower bound in Cut(K) of {Q(C): C a nondegenerate convex polygon}.
roles.uniqueness_theorem_or_counterexample: Unique for a fixed (N,mu), but not determined by the S4+N reduct.
roles.why_not_classical_formula_renaming: The frozen role is an unnormalized optimization invariant of arbitrary norm/valuation planes; it does not mention any privileged shape, center, radius, circumference, or target constant.

roles.choice_dependence: The sign/orientation of a raw generator is intentionally unmarked and not promoted to an invariant.
degeneracies: a later scalar normalization would be extra structure
roles.exact_construction: Let Gen(ker p) be the set of group generators of the infinite cyclic kernel. Take the orbit/class [t] under inversion t~t^{-1}.
roles.existence_theorem_or_failure: Exists because ker(p) is infinite cyclic.
roles.finite_computability: Symbolically exact from a cyclic-group presentation; the S6 model itself is infinite.
roles.invariance_theorem_or_failure: The quotient class is invariant under cover isomorphisms. A raw generator is not invariant under inversion.
roles.role_predicate: x is the unique inversion orbit containing every generator of ker(p).
roles.uniqueness_theorem_or_counterexample: The quotient class is unique; raw generators occur as an inverse pair and are nonunique.
roles.why_not_classical_formula_renaming: It records only the algebraic period-kernel generator class and deliberately withholds any scalar period length or angular unit.
